text.p: The Football Association confirmed on Friday that Liverpool defender Neil Ruddock has been charged with bringing the game into disrepute over an attack on Tottenham chairman Alan Sugar in a Sunday newspaper article.
Ruddock has 14 days in which to request a personal hearing, but is unlikely to receive any support from his club, who have already apologised to Sugar. He now faces a heavy fine from the FA.
Sugar complained to the F.A. after last weekend's story in which Ruddock, who was sold by Spurs to Liverpool in 1993, was quoted as saying Sugar was not running Tottenham as a football club.
